rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for things or people being apart rather than together.

example.english: You two sit in separate seats; don’t sit together.
example.traditional: 你哋分開坐，唔好坐埋一齊。
example.jyutping: nei5 dei6 fan1 hoi1 co5 m4 hou2 co5 maai4 jat1 cai4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for dividing things or people, including saying that something has come apart by itself.

example.english: I separate the cookies into two plates.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoeng1 di1 beng2 fan1 hoi1 loeng5 dip6

rows.note: Use this when separate emphasizes being a standalone or independently functioning unit, rather than merely being apart.

example.english: This flat has a separate kitchen, so you don’t have to share one.
example.traditional: 呢間屋有獨立廚房，唔使同人共用。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 uk1 jau5 duk6 lap6 cyu4 fong2 m4 sai2 tung4 jan4 gung6 jung6

rows.note: Use this when someone or something breaks away from a group, relationship, or affiliation rather than from a physical connection.

example.english: They decided to separate from this organization.
example.jyutping: keoi5 kyut3 ding6 tyut3 lei4 ni1 go3 zou2 zik1

rows.note: Use this for physically disconnecting or breaking a connection, such as a wire, link, or line.

example.english: I had to separate the network cable from the router.
example.traditional: 我要將條網線同個路由器斷開。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jiu3 zoeng1 tiu4 mong5 sin3 tung4 go3 lou6 jau4 hei3 dyun6 hoi1

rows.note: Use this especially when a mixture or substance separates into distinct components, rather than for ordinary people or objects.

example.english: Oil and water will separate if you leave them sitting for a while.
example.traditional: 油同水擺耐咗就會分離。
example.jyutping: jau4 tung4 seoi2 baai2 noi6 zo2 zau6 wui5 fan1 lei4
